title: Nigeria's economy grows 4.43% — its fastest in five years
body: Second-quarter growth was carried by services, telecommunications, finance and agriculture, while the trade surplus doubled to $9.5bn. Non-oil sectors now account for 96% of total output.
source: Semafor Africa · National Bureau of Statistics

title: Nigeria launches $300m distributed renewable energy fund as World Bank commits $25m
body: The Nigeria DRE Fund, co-managed by NSIA and Africa50 with SEforALL, has reached commercial operation, moving from structuring to active capital deployment for mini-grids, solar home systems and storage. The World Bank joined as a founding partner with an initial $25 million IDA commitment. The fund is aligned with Mission 300, the World Bank-AfDB push to connect 300 million Africans to electricity by 2030, and is positioned as a country-level model replicable across Africa.

title: Dangote unveils $46-50bn Vision 2030 expansion; Lamu refinery groundbreaking set for Sept 30
body: At Unstoppable Africa 2026 on the UNGA sidelines, Aliko Dangote announced plans to invest $46-50 billion under the group Vision 2030 strategy, including doubling the Lagos refinery from 700,000 to 1.4 million barrels per day. Kenya President Ruto met Dangote and Africa Finance Corporation in New York to line up financing for the $15-16 billion East Africa Refinery in Lamu, with groundbreaking scheduled September 30 and construction around 30 months.

title: AU commissioner: Africa needs $64bn a year and cross-border power trade to close energy gap
body: African Union Infrastructure and Energy Commissioner Lerato Dorothy Mataboge told the Global Africa Business Initiative in New York that closing Africa electricity access gap, with roughly 600 million people unserved, requires about $64 billion annually. She pushed policy harmonisation and cross-border electricity trade under the African Single Electricity Market (AfSEM) plus a continental energy master plan to coordinate investment in transmission.

title: Africa makes its case for a bigger role on the global stage
body: Leaders from business, government and global institutions convened in New York alongside the 81st UN General Assembly. The UN Secretary-General called for a permanent African seat on the Security Council and for the continent's critical minerals to generate local value and jobs rather than being exported raw.

title: $300m Nigeria Distributed Renewable Energy Fund reaches first close
body: Co-managed by the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority and Africa50, the fund will finance local clean-energy developers — solar mini-grids, home systems and storage — aligned to Mission 300's goal of connecting 300 million Africans to electricity by 2030.

title: Kenya: 90%+ renewable electricity, and a new critical-minerals facility
body: Kenya generates more than 90% of its electricity from renewable sources, and the US backed a critical minerals processing facility in a country holding untapped copper, graphite, lithium and nickel.

title: AfCFTA trade projected to reach $230bn this year
body: Intra-African trade under the Continental Free Trade Area keeps scaling, supported by continental payment rails that shift cross-border settlement away from correspondent banking.

title: Dangote Refinery IPO set to be Africa's largest share sale
body: Nigeria's SEC approved an offering expected to raise around $1.5–1.8bn, with plans to double the refinery's capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day — which would make it the largest single-train refinery in the world.

title: Africa's solar adoption projected to rise 45% this year
body: As energy independence becomes a strategic priority, several countries moved to expand both refining and generation capacity — with renewables adoption rising sharply across the continent.

title: AGOA extended through December 2028
body: Preferential duty-free access to the US market is preserved for eligible sub-Saharan exporters, giving textiles, apparel and agriculture a firmer footing for the next two years.

title: Fintech remains Africa's largest venture sector
body: African start-ups raised $1.35bn in the first half of 2026. Fintech took $556m (41%) and logistics $472m. Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa and Egypt have absorbed roughly 80% of all capital raised since 2019.
